Eon’s last memory from his old life was the screech of tires on wet asphalt, the blinding headlights, and the sickening crunch of metal. Then nothing. No light at the end of the tunnel, no voice of God—just the quiet promise that everything was over.

Until it wasn’t.

He woke up choking on his own spit, small lungs burning, tiny fists flailing. The ceiling above him was not the cracked plaster of his Seoul apartment. It was a vaulted dome of translucent crystal and living gold filigree, carved with constellations that slowly rotated on their own. Soft aurora-like light drifted across the surface like liquid starlight. A gentle chime echoed—some kind of magical smart-home system—and a holographic calendar bloomed in mid-air.

“Year 147 of the Sovereign Era. Third day of the Aether Bloom. Young Master Eon Aetherion, age 3 years, 2 months, 17 days.”

Eon stared. His mouth opened, but only a childish gurgle came out. He lifted his hands—chubby, soft, toddler hands—and felt the weight of a body that was not his. Panic surged, then curiosity, then a cold, crystal-clear understanding.

I… reincarnated. Into a manhwa world. The kind I binged every night after overtime. Monsters, dungeons, classes, levels, status windows… the whole package.

He rolled over, fighting the weakness of infant muscles, and crawled to the edge of an enormous bed draped in silk that shimmered like woven moonlight. The room was the size of his old apartment’s entire floor. Marble floors veined with glowing runes. Floating lanterns shaped like miniature suns. A wall-sized window that wasn’t glass but a transparent force-field offering a view that stole the breath he barely had.

Aetherhaven.

The legendary Sky Citadel of the House of Aetherion.

Floating islands—dozens of them—hovered in perfect formation above an endless sea of clouds. Crystal bridges of pure mana connected towers of obsidian and star-steel that rose like proud spears. Neon holograms in elegant Han-style script advertised everything from S-rank mana potions to limited-edition flying sports cars. Traditional pagoda roofs sat atop skyscrapers that would make Dubai jealous, their eaves carved with protective dragons whose eyes actually tracked movement. Airships the size of cruise liners glided between districts, their hulls emblazoned with the golden crest of a rising sun wrapped in aurora ribbons. Far below the clouds, the mortal world was a distant patchwork of green and gray—continents that looked suspiciously like a slightly rearranged Earth, dotted with empires, kingdoms, republics, and monster-haunted wild zones.

And ruling it all from this impossible height were the Five Sovereign Houses.

Eon’s mind—still adult, still sharp—flashed through fragmented memories that were not his own but belonged to the tiny body he now inhabited. The knowledge poured in like someone had opened a floodgate:

The Five Sovereign Houses—above nations, above laws, above even the gods people pretended to worship.

House of Aetherion — his family. The unchallenged apex. Their military alone outclassed every empire on the planet combined, the way the United States in 2010 outclassed everyone else in sheer projection of power. Their word was veto. Their displeasure was extinction.
House of Pyralis — masters of flame and industrial might.
House of Cryonix — rulers of the frozen north, cold calculation and absolute defense.
